2608.01708.title: PGMem: Tightly Coupled Persona-Memory Graph for Lifelong Personalized Agents
2608.01708.paper_summary: Long-term personalized dialogue agents must track user preferences as their personas evolve. Existing memory systems organize past events well, but store personas as flat profiles detached from the events that justify them. This loose coupling leads to the memory-persona validity gap and the persona-aware retrieval gap. We propose PGMem, a heterogeneous persona-memory graph that connects event and persona nodes through typed provenance and evidence edges, keeping each persona signal traceable to the events that support or revise it. At retrieval time, PGMem expands from query-relevant seeds and ranks signals by evidential validity. Across three benchmarks with small language model backbones, PGMem consistently outperforms summary-based, persona-aware, graph-structured, and agentic memory baselines, and improves performance as the context grows. The source code of PGMem is available at https://github.com/wonjunchoi23/pgmem/
2608.01708.paper_summary_zh: 長期個性化對話代理必須隨著用戶偏好的演變而追蹤其個性。現有的記憶系統很好地組織過去的事件，但將個性存儲為與這些事件無關的平面檔案。這種鬆散的耦合導致了記憶-個性有效性差距和個性感知檢索差距。我們提出了PGMem，一種異質個性-記憶圖，通過類型化的來源和證據邊緣將事件和個性節點連接起來，使每個個性信號可追溯到支持或修訂它的事件。在檢索時，PGMem從與查詢相關的種子擴展，並根據證據有效性對信號進行排名。在三個基準測試中，使用小型語言模型作為骨幹，PGMem始終優於基於摘要的、個性感知的、圖結構的和代理記憶基準，並隨著上下文的增長而提高性能。PGMem的源代碼可在https://github.com/wonjunchoi23/pgmem/獲得。
